class_guess: Base-4 counter on 10-regions in a 100 sea; overflow eats the left wall and spawns a digit at the right
summary: Exact base-4 counter: digits are 10-regions in a 100 sea; a mod-3 field law keeps merges clean; no halt to 1e15.
mechanism: Tape at every C-record: 0^inf <wall> W^a D W^f ... D W^c 11 C> 0^inf, with W = 100 and digits D(m,p) = X (10)^m Y (m even, X in {10,11}, Y in {10,00}, phase p = 2x+y). One sweep adds 1 to this base-4 counter from the right; phases 1->2 and 3->0 shift the digit one W left; the right field gains 1 W.

Every interior field keeps J = f + 2pL + floor(pR/2) - floor(pL/2) = 0 (mod 3), so a dying field always merges its two digits into one D(m+m'+2) and never goes negative. Digits are born at the right end on overflows and merge as they drift left: 10 digits at 1e14.

Overflow: [10100] W^a -> [] W^a and [] W^a -> [10100] W^(a-2) (+ a birth). When the far-left field runs out, the wall eats the top digit through a finite remnant family. The three starts enter the same language by step 20,600, differing only in the far-left field; an exact sweep simulator matches the C core at 1e11 on all three and reaches 1e14 with no halt (82: 1e15).

rules.name: R1 increment (p = 0, 1, 2)
rules.to: L W^(a-s) D(m,p+1) W^(c+1+s) 11 C> 0^inf, s = 1 if p = 1 else 0

rules.name: R2 carry (p = 3)
rules.from: L W^a D(m',q) W^f D(m,3) W^c 11 C> 0^inf
rules.to: R1 applied to D(m',q) with W^f as its right field, D(m,3) -> D(m,0) shifted 1 W left; right field c+2
rules.cases: repeats leftward through every digit at phase 3

rules.name: J invariant and merges
rules.from: interior field W^f between D(.,pL) and D(.,pR) with f + 2pL + floor(pR/2) - floor(pL/2) = 0 (mod 3)
rules.to: J stays 0 under R1/R2; a field reaching 0 is followed by D(m,2x+0)D(m',0+y) = D(m+m'+2, 2x+y), never by a negative field

rules.name: O1/O2 overflow
rules.from: 0^inf [10100 | empty] W^a (all digits at phase 3) W^c 11 C> 0^inf
rules.cases: a >= 4; every digit shifts 1 W left; birth or no birth both stay in the language

rules.name: Wall eats the top digit
rules.cases: 80 small-field families (wall x a in 0..4 x m in 0..6 x 2 field sizes): all return to a clean wall, none halts

template.diff: different table; same architecture (digits with take/give/carry over a periodic word W, segRLs wall and one-digit lemmas)
template.note: mxdys's Sk1Counter matches our sweep rules (one digit step = segRLs with take/give/carry; W traversal = wall lemma). Its endgame does not: TM17 runs an accelerated simulation until a glider (translated cycle); ours grows forever (fields 3*2^k, 10 digits at 1e14), so the endgame must be a closed invariant (as in our #30), not a glider check.

strategy: Finish stage 1: write the wall/remnant case table as affine rules and run an exhaustive closure check of the candidate language L (J-valid fields, even digits, wall grammar). Then proof.md: one closed-language argument for L plus three entry lemmas (82, 464, 722).
risks: The wall grammar is only seen to 1e14: the remnant prefixes (11, 1, empty, 10100, 1011) and collision chains need a complete, proved table.
Formal size: the Sk1Counter-style lemmas exist upstream, but the closed-set argument over arbitrary digit lists is new work (#30 was 1,726 lines).
Owner risk: the class is mxdys's (Sk1Machines.v); ask in #bb6 before stage 2.
